title: BCIT Basic Guard Duty
description: This dataset contains EEG, eye-tracking, and behavioral data from the Basic Guard Duty study, part of a larger project examining sustained vigilance in realistic task settings. Participants performed a two-alternative forced-choice ID verification task, judging the validity of replica identification cards presented at varying rates, while high-density EEG (256+8 channels) and eye-tracking data were recorded. The task was designed to probe attentional and vigilance dynamics under varying cognitive load, complementing companion driving tasks not included in this release.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a BioSemi 256(+8) channel system (plus 4 eye and 2 mastoid channels) at 1024 Hz sampling rate. Eye tracking was performed using a Sensomotoric Instruments (SMI) REDEYE250 system. Participants completed a guard duty task involving serial presentation of replica ID cards paired with reference images, requiring allow/deny access decisions across ten 5-minute blocks with varying stochastic presentation rates (1–25 IDs/min). Additional questionnaire data (fatigue and sleepiness scales) were collected but are not included in this dataset.
